channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran Navy Claims Two Oil Tankers Exploded in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Navy announced that two oil tankers exploded at the entrance to the port of Khassab and east of the Strait of Hormuz. The tankers were reportedly traveling on an "unauthorized route" and exploded after hitting naval mines. U.S. Central Command stated the Strait of Hormuz is clear of mines.

item.title: Afghan Hindu Elders Meet with Taliban Governor in Khost
item.description: Several elders from the Hindu community in Khost met with the Taliban governor of the province to present their problems, demands, and suggestions. While details of the discussions were not released, property غصب, discrimination, and religious freedom restrictions are significant challenges for the Hindu and Sikh communities in Afghanistan.

item.title: Osh Completes 1.5 km Road Renovation Near 'Dostuk' Border Crossing
item.description: Osh has opened a 1.5 km section of Osh Street for traffic, from Zhetimishov Street to the roundabout near the 'Dostuk' border crossing. The renovation widened the road to 24 meters with four lanes, added new asphalt, sidewalks, and drainage. This is the first major repair since the Soviet era. New trees were planted, and residents displaced by the expansion received new homes.

item.title: US Backs Iraqi PM's Efforts to Assert Central Government Authority
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has expressed support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaydi's efforts to extend the central government's authority across Iraq. This includes stopping oil smuggling, ending corruption, and ensuring the government has exclusive control over weapons. The statement follows an announcement by an Iraqi government spokesperson detailing over $100 billion in damages from Kurdistan's oil exports outside central government control.

item.title: Bishkek to Begin Construction of National Equestrian Sports Complex
item.description: Bishkek City Hall has commenced the construction of a National Equestrian Sports Complex near Belek village in the Sokuluk district. The complex will span 114 hectares and include a 10,000-seat hippodrome and a 25,000-seat arena for Kok Boru competitions. Construction is planned for completion within 1.5 years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Procedures for State Border Protection Agency Cooperation
item.description: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a new instruction on the interaction procedures between the State Border Service and other government bodies, presidential representatives, and local administrations. The document aims to enhance border security and coordinate inter-agency actions. Previous regulations from 2013 have been repealed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Railway History: From Early Beginnings to Modern Challenges
item.description: The history of railways in Kazakhstan began in Oral, but the West Kazakhstan region is now one of the most vulnerable and least utilized railway areas. Early lines from the late 19th century are still in use, with historical stations reflecting Eastern architectural styles. Major projects in the early 20th century aimed to connect oil and fish resources but were halted by war and revolution.

item.title: Kazakh Man Champions Rights of Orphans After Personal Tragedy
item.description: Ruslan Tursybekov leads the "Don't Remain Silent, Orphan Child" foundation, advocating for orphans' rights. Having lost his mother at seven, he understands their struggles and is dedicated to improving legislation and supporting orphaned youth. His work aims to give hope and opportunities to those without parental care.

item.title: UN Experts Demand Pakistan Investigate Civilian Killings in PoJK
item.description: UN human rights experts have formally requested Pakistan to investigate civilian deaths in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). At least 96 protesters were reportedly killed since June 2026, with many victims aged 15-35. Experts emphasize that peaceful protest should not be equated with terrorism and firearms should not be used to disperse assemblies.

item.title: Hamas Leader's Last Surviving Son Escapes Israeli Strike in Gaza
item.description: The last surviving son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya, Izzeldeen al-Hayya, and his family survived an Israeli air strike in Gaza. Several relatives were injured. Hamas condemned the attack, calling it an assassination attempt and accusing Israel of undermining a ceasefire. Meanwhile, separate Israeli attacks killed four Palestinians elsewhere in the enclave.

item.title: UK Army Chief Visits Pakistan Border Amid Regional Security Concerns
item.description: General Sir Roly Walker, UK Chief of the General Staff, visited a Pakistani border post along the Afghanistan frontier. He held talks with Pakistan's military leadership on regional developments, defense relations, and counterterrorism. The visit aimed to enhance understanding of Pakistan's security challenges and regional stability, reinforcing bilateral defense cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize $200,000 in Attempted Currency Smuggling
item.description: Kazakhstan's Border Service intercepted 59 attempts to illegally export currency totaling over 508 million tenge between November 16-25. At the Korday checkpoint, a foreigner was caught trying to smuggle $200,000 (91 million tenge). Another citizen was found with 4.4 million rubles in luggage at the Aktobe region border.

item.title: UN Warns Taliban Restrictions on Female Aid Workers Harm Afghan Women and Girls
item.description: The UN warns that Taliban restrictions on female humanitarian workers prevent women and girls in Afghanistan from accessing essential aid, information, and protection. The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) stressed that female colleagues are crucial for assessing needs and that no woman should be excluded from assistance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Boost Meat Production by 400,000 Tons by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to increase livestock feed production from 48 million to 90 million tons by 2030, creating conditions to produce an additional 400,000 tons of meat. This initiative, presented to President Mirziyoyev, seeks to meet growing demand, lower production costs, and stabilize prices for meat and dairy products.

item.title: New Monkeypox Cases Detected in Russia Among Travelers
item.description: Russian health officials confirmed a third case of monkeypox in St. Petersburg within 24 hours, involving a resident who returned from a trip to Thailand. Two other infected individuals were hospitalized the previous day. Patients are in stable condition, and contact tracing and disinfection are underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Enters Silence Day Ahead of Local Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan has entered a silence day, prohibiting all campaign activities to allow citizens to make their choices without pressure. Previously published campaign materials remain online but cannot be further promoted. The local elections are scheduled for November 29, with 3,447 mandates available.

item.title: Rosstat Data Leak Reveals 510-1375 Kazakh Citizens Died in Russian Army
item.description: A leak of Rosstat data, attributed to Belarusian hacker group 'Cyber Partisans', suggests between 510 and 1375 Kazakh citizens may have died while serving in the Russian army. The data, covering deaths from 2021 to September 2026, indicates nearly 59% of foreign casualties in the Russian military are from five Central Asian countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets New Electricity Production Record Amidst Regional Energy Security Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan recorded a new historical high in electricity production, reaching 17,356 MW on November 16. This achievement comes as a massive power outage in August served as a stark reminder of energy security importance in Central Asia. Despite increased production, the risk of widespread blackouts remains due to system stability issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan's External Debt Stands at $187.9 Billion, Relative Share Decreases
item.description: As of July 1, Kazakhstan's external debt reached $187.9 billion, an increase of $4.8 billion since the beginning of the year. However, its share in the gross domestic product decreased from 59.9% to 56.6%, indicating that the economy is growing faster than its debt. The government's portion of this debt is less than half.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Civil Code by End of 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Civil Code, in effect for over thirty years, will be updated. President Tokayev has tasked the development and adoption of a new Civil Code by the end of 2027. A working group comprising lawmakers, government officials, legal experts, and business representatives has begun its work on the revision.

item.title: Turkmenistan Parliament Approves 2027 State Budget Law and 2025 Budget Execution Decision
item.description: The Mejlis of Turkmenistan has approved the Law on the State Budget for 2027 and a decision on the execution of the State Budget for 2025. These legislative acts were adopted during the parliament's recent session. The parliament also discussed ongoing work to improve the country's legislation in line with modern requirements.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Former State Security Service officials sentenced to lengthy prison terms
item.description: Uzbekistan's Military Court sentenced former officials of the State Security Service (SSS) on November 27. Former deputy head General Gayratilla Yoziyev received 15 years, and former head of SSS Internal Security Colonel Alijon Ashurov received 17 years. Other officials were also sentenced to 15 to 17 years. Yoziyev was found guilty of extortion, illegal detention, and abuse of power.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism
item.description: Uzbekistan has announced the launch of the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism (2027) in Tashkent. This initiative, developed by Uzbekistan and supported by over 80 countries, was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2024. The event was attended by UN Tourism Secretary-General and representatives from more than 45 nations.

item.title: Moscow to Increase Migrant Work Permit Fees from January 1, 2027
item.description: Moscow authorities will raise the cost of work permits for migrants starting January 1, 2027. The Moscow City Duma approved amendments to tax legislation, increasing the monthly fee. This decision is attributed to rising average salaries in sectors popular among foreigners. Similar increases are expected in other regions.

item.title: Turkmenistan Parliament Approves 2025 State Budget Execution Report
item.description: The Mejlis of Turkmenistan has decided to approve the execution of the State Budget for 2025, with revenues amounting to 139,299,374.6 billion manats and expenditures totaling 138,655,834.4 billion manats. The decision was signed by the Speaker of the Mejlis, D. Gulmanova, in Ashgabat on November 25, 2026.

item.title: Turkmenistan Highlights Significance of New Environmental Initiatives at International Summits
item.description: An international conference in Ashgabat focused on the importance of new environmental initiatives proposed by the President of Turkmenistan at UN summits on biodiversity and climate change. Discussions involved international partners on implementing these proposals, with participation from diplomats and media representatives. The initiatives presented at COP17 and COP31 garnered significant global attention, demonstrating the effectiveness of Turkmenistan's 'green' diplomacy.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Parliament Granted Observer Status in CIS Parliamentary Assembly
item.description: A conference in Ashgabat discussed the significance of Turkmenistan's parliament receiving observer status in the CIS Parliamentary Assembly. This development is seen as a crucial step in strengthening interstate cooperation and the international legal framework. The conference also highlighted the UN General Assembly's declaration of 2028 as the 'International Year of Law'.

item.title: Cameras Found in School Toilet in Atyrau, Kazakhstan; Data Breaches Also Reported
item.description: Prosecutors in Atyrau, Kazakhstan, discovered cameras in a school toilet, compromising the privacy of over 1,400 students. The regional prosecutor's office also reported other violations, including personal data breaches affecting over 4,000 children across the region. Violators have been held accountable and rights restored.

item.title: Rustam Emomali's Increased Public Appearances Alongside Father Fuels Succession Speculation
item.description: Rustam Emomali, the eldest son of Tajikistan's president, is appearing more frequently with his father at official events and on state television. This increased visibility, including jointly welcoming Russian President Putin, has intensified discussions about potential power transition ahead of next year's presidential election.

item.title: Jizzakh Water Official Arrested for Promising to Erase Debt
item.description: An employee of "Jizzakh Suv Ta'minoti" JSC has been apprehended for allegedly demanding 9 million soums. The official reportedly promised to erase a 100 million soum water debt for an entrepreneur and install a new water meter in exchange for the bribe.

item.title: Kazatomprom Clarifies Official Status of Second Arrested Employee
item.description: Kazatomprom has clarified the official status of an employee arrested by the National Security Committee. The company stated that the arrested individual is a chief manager of a department, not a top executive. The National Security Committee reported the arrest of Kuanych Omurbekov and chief manager Baikulov, suspecting them of involvement in a corruption scheme.

item.title: Kazatomprom Clarifies Status of Second Suspect in Criminal Case
item.description: Kazatomprom has clarified the position of E. Baikulova, the second individual mentioned in a criminal case by the National Security Committee. The company stated Baikulova is a chief manager in a department, not a top executive. The clarification comes after media reports suggested another top manager was arrested. Both Baikulova and a former chief production director were arrested for two months.

item.title: Kazakhstan Conducts Security Checks on Polling Stations Ahead of Maslikhat Elections
item.description: Over 10,000 polling stations across Kazakhstan are undergoing security checks in preparation for the maslikhat elections scheduled for November 29. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirmed that anti-terrorism protection requirements are being verified. Police will maintain public order on election day.

item.title: Harvard Analysts Develop Four Scenarios for Russia's Future by 2030
item.description: Harvard analysts have developed four scenarios outlining potential political and economic changes in Russia by 2030. The study examines the possible outcomes of the war in Ukraine, Russia's international standing, and the future of Putin's leadership, assessing which scenario is most likely to occur.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Changes to Judge Disciplinary Commission Structure
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering amendments to the Law "On Bodies of Judicial Self-Governance" to reform the disciplinary commission of the Judicial Council. The proposed changes aim to include lawyers, legal scholars, and human rights defenders alongside judges, enhancing accountability and transparency in disciplinary proceedings against judges.

item.title: Uzbekistan Unveils New Transport Strategy Focused on Roads and Investment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed Uzbekistan's new transport strategy, emphasizing quality roads, significant investments, and international integration. He visited a road construction research center and met with investors, highlighting the importance of scientific research and modern technologies in the transport sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Coal Enterprises Request Government Permission for Summer Exports
item.description: Coal mining enterprises in Kyrgyzstan's Sulyukta are seeking government permission to export coal during the summer months. Currently, export is restricted, and companies prioritize supplying the domestic market in autumn and winter. Summer exports would help prevent coal degradation from prolonged storage and address falling domestic demand.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Registration for Citizenship Test Applicants
item.description: Kazakhstan begins accepting applications for the citizenship test on November 27. The National Testing Center will receive applications until December 7, with the test scheduled for December 8. Applicants can register via the National Testing Center's website or app. The test covers Kazakh language, Constitution basics, and history.

item.title: Taliban Security Commission Meets Under Leader Akhundzada
item.description: The Taliban's security commission convened a meeting led by the group's leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. The meeting was held at the Taliban-run Arg, according to a statement from the office.

item.title: Kazakhstan Court Sentences Activist Sanjar Bokayev; Over 13,000 Foreign Fighters Die in Ukraine
item.description: A court in Almaty has issued a verdict in the case of activist Sanjar Bokayev. Over 13,000 individuals from Central Asian countries fighting for Russia in Ukraine have died, including Kazakh citizens. The prosecutor's office issued a warning ahead of the maslikhat elections.
